supersedes: R082w-memory-budget-v3.json (for the R112 limits; v1 to v3 stay as they are)
acceptanceStatus: not-accepted: the modeled worst case with a GLB export is over the owner's 3.75 GiB ceiling (owner decision open)
measuredScope: Software only: Release, static, command-line build (SKETCHYUP_BUILD_DESKTOP=OFF, so no viewport, no llvmpipe frame figures). Peaks are process peak RSS. Not hardware evidence; D-091 stays open.

buildAndRun.configuration: CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release, SKETCHYUP_BUILD_DESKTOP=OFF, SKETCHYUP_BUILD_CLI=ON, SKETCHYUP_BUILD_IFC=OFF, SKETCHYUP_SHARED_LIBS=OFF, SKETCHYUP_NATIVE_FIXTURES_IN_ALL=OFF
buildAndRun.harness: tests/snapshot_glb_limits_benchmark.cpp (new, EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL) and sketchyup-cli; export mode prints resident memory before and after the GLB export

reason: R112 raises the read-snapshot budget from 256 MiB to 512 MiB (owner approval 2026-11-06) and the GLB visible-face cap from 100,000 to 600,000, with the manifest bound at 192 MiB. The snapshot budget is admission only (a snapshot shares records), so v3's resident terms do not change. The GLB export at 600,000 faces adds a transient that v3 did not model: about 278 MiB above the resident model. With v3's 3.72 GiB (hardware delta included) the modeled worst case with an export is 3.99 GiB, over the 3.75 GiB ceiling and 14 MiB under the 4 GiB cap. The brief's stop rule applies, so the pull request is not opened.

shapes.spheres-at-cap: three closed 100,000-face spheres, each placed twice; unique 300,000 faces, 150,006 vertices, 450,000 edges; materialized 600,000 faces, 300,012 vertices, 900,000 edges
shapes.strips-at-limits: three strip definitions (99,998, 99,998 and 98,004 triangles) and a 2,000-face sphere placed 100 times; unique 300,000 faces, 299,008 vertices, 599,003 edges; materialized 498,000 faces, 398,206 vertices, 896,003 edges. Edges bind before materialized faces with smooth edges.

strips-at-limits-textured.variant: tex=3:0 (all sphere faces, 200,000 copies), tex=0:25000 and tex=1:25000 (50,000 strip faces)

exportGlb.error: Render snapshot exceeds the read-snapshot budget

catalogImport.composition: base of two spheres placed twice (400,000 materialized, 200,000 unique) plus one-sphere entry (100,000 faces) imported
catalogImport.note: a catalog import adds a new definition each time, so it cannot raise a placement count; the 600,000-face model is measured by its container instead

desktopExportOnLoadedViewport.answer: yes, through the Blender render path (src/integrations/blender_job.cpp calls exportGlb and writeGlbExport on the document while the viewport holds its payload)
desktopExportOnLoadedViewport.reason: the desktop build is not compiled here; the transient was measured on the command-line export, which runs the same exportGlb and writeGlbExport

limitsChangedBy: glbManifestByteLimit 128 MiB to 192 MiB (blender_worker.py bound to match)
hardwareRequirement: Fresh Intel and AMD reruns per docs/M9_HARDWARE_SESSION.md section 1 remain required; the ADR 0161 waiver applies as it did to v2 and v3.

ownerDecisionOpen.question: The modeled worst case with a GLB export at 600,000 faces is 3.99 GiB, over the 3.75 GiB ceiling.
options: accept the modeled peak over the ceiling, 14 MiB under the 4 GiB job cap (not recommended)
lower the GLB visible-face cap to about 77,000 faces, so the transient fits the 35.7 MiB left under the ceiling
reduce the export transient (a streamed manifest writer, or a smaller per-face manifest record, which changes the format)
keep 600,000 for the command-line export only, and bound the desktop render path so the viewport and the export do not stand together at the worst case
